proposition.claim:
Let \(P_{n,d}\) denote the projective space of nonzero degree-\(d\) homogeneous polynomials in \(n+1\) complex variables, and let \(\Delta_{n,d}\) be the discriminant of polynomials whose projective zero equation is singular. In dimension \(n=1\), the measure \(\mu([p])\) is the probability measure assigning to each projective root its multiplicity divided by \(d\); see pp. 45–47 and Theorem 3.8, p. 69.

Definition 5.1, p. 77, requires \[\mu\circ\gamma\in AC^2([0,1];\mathcal P_2(\mathbb{CP}^{n})),
 \qquad
 \mathcal E(\gamma)=\int_0^1|\dot\mu_t|^2\,dt.\] The speed is measured using the ambient \(W_2\) distance. The formal definition of \(AC^2\) in Definition 2.2, p. 57, supplies an \(L^2\) upper gradient for distances between every two times. Thus an almost-everywhere metric speed with divergent square integral rules out admissibility. References below to infinite energy use the extended-energy convention; they do not assert that a nonadmissible curve belongs to the domain of Definition 5.1.

Paraphrase: For every continuous semialgebraic gamma:[0,1]->P_n,d starting on Delta and outside Delta for all t in(0,1], there exists a positive integer m with gamma(s^m) of finite W2 energy.
